title: Linear Programming I (cross-listed MATH 561, TO 518)

gradingBreakdown.component: Quizzes (10, need 5/10 correct for full quiz credit)

weeklyTopics: Formulating mathematical optimization models: decision variables, parameters, objectives, constraints
Algebraic and geometric interpretations of linear programs (LPs)
The Primal Simplex method for solving LPs
Primal-dual relationship of an LP and complementary slackness
Integer programs (IPs): formulation, branch-and-bound, cutting-plane algorithms, totally unimodular structures
Linear optimization approaches: decomposition, Lagrangian relaxation, column generation
workloadNotes: Graduate-level optimization course, asynchronous lecture delivery via Canvas recordings. Homework done in groups of 1-3 (bonus 5 extra credit points for groups of 3), submitted as typed LaTeX with strict late penalties (80% at <24h late, 60% at <48h, 40% at <72h, zero beyond). Weekly quizzes. Group project (1-3 students) applying course techniques to a real optimization problem: LaTeX report (6-10 pages), 6-10 slide presentation, individual contribution statement, and Q&A to verify collaboration. Two take-home exams, no makeup dates offered.
prerequisitesText: Linear algebra (matrix analysis, row/column operations, solving linear systems); ability to write mathematical proofs and to code.
textbooks: Bazaraa, Jarvis, and Sherali, Linear Programming and Network Flows, 4th ed., Wiley, 2010 (optional)
Jon Lee, A First Course in Linear Optimization, 2nd ed. (optional, freely available)
